title: AI Maze Explorer
blurb: Trap a robot in a maze, set the rewards, and watch it teach itself the way out — no path required.
objectives: How rewards — not instructions — shape what an AI does
Why a wrong reward leads to weird behavior

glossary.def: Points the AI gets (or loses) for what it does. Good things give points, bad things take them away.
Learning by trying things over and over and keeping what earns the most reward.
The thing that's learning and making choices — here, the little robot.
One full attempt — from the start until the robot reaches the goal or gives up.

steps.title: A robot in a maze
steps.body:
A little robot is dropped into a maze. It has **no map** and nobody tells it the way out.

All you can do is decide what's **good** and what's **bad**: reaching the exit feels great, bumping a wall hurts, and wandering forever is a waste. Then the robot tries… and tries… and tries — and slowly figures the rest out itself.

steps.title: First try?
steps.prompt: When the robot first wakes up in the maze, what will it do?
steps.afterPick: At the start it knows *nothing*, so it mostly bumbles — bumping walls and backtracking. The magic is what happens after lots of tries. Let's watch. →

steps.title: Set the rewards, then train
steps.youWillDo: set the rewards and train the robot
steps.body:
Set your **rewards** (reaching the exit, hitting a wall, taking a step), then press **Train** a few times and **Watch it go**. Early on it's clumsy; after enough rounds it finds a clean path.

When that works, try the **Bad rewards** button — make hitting walls a *good* thing — and watch what the robot decides to do.

steps.title: You never drew the path
steps.body:
Notice what you actually did: you **never told the robot the route**. You only said what was worth points.

The robot found the path by **trial and error** — keeping the moves that earned reward and dropping the ones that didn't. That's **reinforcement learning**.

steps.title: What did the rewards do?
steps.question: When you made *hitting a wall* give points, why did the robot start crashing into walls on purpose?
choices: It does whatever earns the most reward — and you told it walls pay
It got scared of the exit
Mazes are too hard for AI
steps.explain: Exactly — the robot chases reward. If you reward the wrong thing, you get the wrong behavior. The reward *is* the instruction.

steps.title: Say it your way
steps.prompt: In your own words: how did the robot learn the maze without being given the path?

recall.question: Reinforcement learning means the AI learns mainly by…
recall.explain: Try → get reward → keep what works. Over and over.

steps.title: Where this shows up 🎉
steps.body:
You just used **reinforcement learning** — the same idea behind:

- game AIs that get scary-good at chess and video games
- warehouse and delivery **robots** finding routes
- self-driving cars learning to steer

The big lesson: **you shape behavior with rewards, not step-by-step orders** — so picking the right reward is everything. **Next up:** clean the messy data that AI learns from.
